reading.title: When the taxi apps arrived
reading.text: Ride-hailing apps are a classic example of disruptive technology. When they arrived in Jakarta, protests by traditional taxi drivers erupted almost overnight, and traffic in the city centre was disrupted for days. Many small taxi firms went bankrupt within two years. Supporters of the apps argued that the old licensing system had been corrupt, with permits sold to friends of officials. Others worried about the abrupt end of a stable profession. Today, most drivers work for the apps, and their income can be interrupted at any moment by a change in the algorithm.
